new_candidates.duration: From adoption at a July 13, 2026 special meeting through November 30, 2026.
new_candidates.legal_basis: El Dorado City Commission resolution, adopted 4-1 at a special meeting on 2026-07-13 (resolution number not confirmed in sources retrieved), providing an interim moratorium on the development of data centers and battery energy storage systems.
new_candidates.trigger: A citizen-initiated petition (certified 2026-06-25 by the Butler County Clerk) sought to adopt an ordinance prohibiting 'high-impact' data centers (>10 MW peak load or >100,000 gal/day water draw) and Tier 2/Tier 3 battery energy storage systems; the City Commission voted to seek a declaratory judgment on whether the petition was a valid citizen-initiative subject, and adopted the interim moratorium to hold the status quo while that litigation proceeds.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; runs through 2026-11-30 absent further action. The underlying citizen-petition litigation (declaratory judgment sought from the District Court of Butler County) remained pending as of the sources retrieved.
new_candidates.affected_projects: No pending data center or BESS development proposal identified in sources retrieved; the moratorium is explicitly framed as holding the status quo during the petition litigation.
new_candidates.outcome: Suspends development of data centers and battery storage systems in El Dorado through Nov. 30, 2026, 'demonstrat[ing] the City Commission's willingness to allow the process to proceed without considering a development proposal for the uses described in the petition ordinance' while the city seeks a declaratory judgment on the petition's validity.

evidence.title: Official Statement on Decision Regarding Citizen-Initiated Petition
evidence.supports: Official city statement: at the July 13, 2026 special meeting, the City Commission voted to seek a declaratory judgment on the citizen petition and also adopted a resolution imposing a moratorium on data center and battery storage development through November 30, 2026.
evidence.quote: In addition to the decision to seek a declaratory judgment, the City Commission also adopted a resolution providing a moratorium on the development of data centers and battery storage systems. The moratorium extends through November 30, 2026...

evidence.title: El Dorado, KS City Commission - Jul 13, 2026
evidence.supports: Confirms the moratorium was approved 4-1 at the same special meeting where the commission voted 5-0 to seek a declaratory judgment on the citizen petition.
evidence.quote: Instead, a motion declaring the petition invalid and seeking a declaratory judgment passed unanimously, 5-0, and the commission followed with an interim development moratorium covering data centers and battery energy storage systems, approved 4-1.

new_candidates.notes: The underlying citizen-initiated petition ordinance (a permanent ban) is a separate, not-yet-adopted instrument now heading toward possible city commission action or a special election depending on the pending court ruling; per the codebook's guidance on permanent bans, only the enacted interim moratorium is recorded here as a candidate.

new_candidates.legal_basis: South Hutchinson City Council ordinance, adopted unanimously at the May 26, 2026 council meeting (ordinance number not confirmed in sources retrieved).
new_candidates.trigger: A surge of companies proposing data centers nationally prompted the city to act proactively and cautiously before creating permanent rules; this was reported as the first pause on data center/BESS development in the eastern part of Reno County.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; runs through 2027-05-26 absent further action. new_candidates.outcome: One-year pause on data center and battery energy storage system development within South Hutchinson city limits and its extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction, directing the planning commission and staff to review zoning regulations, research other municipalities' standards, and report findings by the end of the moratorium period.

evidence.title: South Hutchinson places moratorium while seeking input on data centers

evidence.quote: During its May 26 meeting, the South Hutch City Council unanimously voted to adopt a one-year moratorium on data centers and battery energy storage systems, or BESS, within city limits and its extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction.

evidence.title: South Hutch puts halt on data centers, BESS, passes moratorium

new_candidates.legal_basis: Shawnee County Board of County Commissioners resolution, adopted 2-1 on 2026-08-13 (Commissioners Kevin Cook and Aaron Mays in favor, Commissioner Bill Riphahn opposed; filed by the County Counselor on Cook's behalf); the resolution's 'Data Center' definition incorporates Shawnee County Home Rule Resolution No. HR-2026003.
new_candidates.trigger: A pending Compass Datacenters Conditional Use Permit application (filed 2026-07-24; found incomplete by county Land Use & Development staff on 2026-08-04) drew public controversy; Commissioner Cook cited a resident's concern about a lack of transparency and wanted to prevent any application from being approved before the board completes its review of county data-center regulations.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; runs through 2027-02-17. The resolution does not stop the pending Compass Datacenters application from being reviewed/evaluated or from a Planning Commission public hearing, but bars the Board of County Commissioners from any final approval/denial until the moratorium ends; the county may resume accepting new data center applications beginning Feb. 18, 2027 absent a further resolution.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Compass Datacenters' pending Conditional Use Permit application near Topeka (filed July 24, 2026); the county may continue reviewing/evaluating that application during the moratorium but the Board cannot take final action on it until Feb. 18, 2027 or later.
new_candidates.outcome: Six-month pause on final Board action on data center land-use applications in Shawnee County (new applications may still be filed and reviewed by staff/Planning Commission, but not finally approved or denied) while the county studies its data-center regulations and hires an outside engineering firm.

evidence.title: Shawnee County halts new data center projects for 6 months
evidence.supports: Detailed report: 2-1 vote on Aug. 13, 2026 adopting the resolution; describes its scope (no final action on data center land-use applications, including the pending Compass Datacenters CUP, until Feb. 17, 2027); cites the Data Center definition from Shawnee County Home Rule Resolution No. HR-2026003.
evidence.quote: The six-month moratorium period will expire on Feb. 17, 2027. It took effect Aug. 13. ... The Board of County Commissioners shall not approve, deny, or otherwise take final action on the case of Compass Data Centers.

evidence.title: Shawnee County commissioners approve temporary moratorium for new data center applications
evidence.supports: Independent confirmation of the 2-1 vote (Cook and Mays in favor, Riphahn opposed) and that Compass Datacenters may still resubmit its application during the moratorium.
evidence.quote: Shawnee County commissioners voted 2-1 Thursday to put a temporary moratorium in place for data center applications until next year.

new_candidates.notes: This is a narrower 'no final action' moratorium rather than a blanket application-acceptance freeze; it is nonetheless framed by the county and by news coverage as a moratorium.

new_candidates.duration: Structured as 12 months per covered category, staggered: data centers expire 2027-07-30, battery energy storage systems expire 2028-07-30, and renewable energy facilities (e.g., wind, solar) expire 2029-07-30; the resolution as a whole 'shall ... remain in full force ... until July 30, 2029.'
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution # 073026, signed and passed 2026-07-30 by Chairman Kenny Roelofsen and Vice Chair Lynn Peterson, citing K.S.A. 12-741 et seq. and K.S.A. 19-101 et seq. police power; excludes uses already defined/enabled under Article 21 of the county zoning regulations and off-grid, on-site residential/commercial renewable installations.
new_candidates.trigger: The county's Comprehensive Plan would generally allow incorporating provisions for data centers, BESS, and alternative energy technology into zoning regulations, but commissioners wanted a strategic pause to evaluate potential impacts on current and future property owners before adopting standards; no applications for these uses had been filed as of the July 2026 Planning Commission recommendation.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; the data-center-specific component runs through 2027-07-30, with BESS and renewable-energy components running longer (through 2028-07-30 and 2029-07-30 respectively) under the same resolution.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None identified as pending in the resolution or sources retrieved.
new_candidates.outcome: Suspends acceptance/processing of Conditional Use Permit applications and construction/erection permits for commercial data centers, BESS, and renewable energy projects (other than those already covered by Article 21 of the zoning code) in unincorporated Dickinson County, directing the Planning and Zoning Board to review and update the zoning regulations for each use category over its respective term.

evidence.title: Resolution # 073026 (signed)
evidence.supports: Full signed resolution text establishing the staggered 12-month-per-category moratorium on data centers, BESS, and renewable energy technology, with the July 30, 2027/2028/2029 expiration dates for each category and the July 30, 2029 overall term.
evidence.quote: The Dickinson County Planning and Zoning Board is directed to review and update the Dickinson County Zoning Regulations for a period of three (3) years, or 12 months for each of the following: Data Centers to expire on July 30, 2027, Battery Energy Storage Systems to expire on July 30, 2028 and Renewable energy facilities to expire on July 30, 2029...

evidence.title: Dickinson County Approves Three-Year Moratorium On Data Centers, Battery Storage And Renewable Energy Projects

evidence.quote: Roelofsen said the county will focus on one of the three areas per year, with the moratorium on each area ending after that year.

new_candidates.duration: 24 months from adoption or until the city repeals it, whichever comes first (2026-07-14 through approximately 2028-07-14).
new_candidates.legal_basis: Lawrence City Commission action, adopted unanimously (5-0) on 2026-07-14, imposing a 24-month moratorium on data center uses within city limits alongside initiation of two Land Development Code text amendments (one requiring a special use permit for data centers instead of by-right development, one directing staff to study water/environmental, energy, utility-cost, noise/light, and setback issues).
new_candidates.trigger: The current Land Development Code allowed data centers in industrial districts by right, with no special approval required; a large crowd of residents urged restrictions, and commissioners wanted time for planning staff to develop new rules (a 12-month option was considered but the commission chose 24 months 'to ensure planning staff had more time'). No specific data center proposal was pending in Lawrence at adoption.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; runs through approximately 2028-07-14 or until repealed. As of a Sept. 21, 2026 follow-up report, the Planning Commission was recommending additional layers to the data-center approval process as part of the same text-amendment process begun in July.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None identified as pending at adoption; director of planning and development Jeff Crick said he was not aware of any proposals to develop a data center in Lawrence.
new_candidates.outcome: 24-month freeze on data center uses within Lawrence city limits while planning staff draft a special-use-permit requirement and study issues (water, energy/utility costs, noise, light, setbacks) for a new data center ordinance; includes a narrow property-owner exception process reviewed against the intent of the pending text amendment.

evidence.title: Lawrence City Commission starts process of developing data center rules, imposes 24-month moratorium
evidence.supports: Detailed report of the July 14, 2026 unanimous vote imposing a 24-month moratorium on data center uses and initiating two text amendments (special use permit requirement; study of impacts), including quotes from the mayor, vice mayor, deputy city attorney, and planning director.
evidence.quote: The City Commission on Tuesday, after hearing from a crowd of advocates, voted unanimously to initiate two text amendments on data centers in the city's Land Development Code and to impose a 24-month moratorium on data center uses within the city limits... It will last for 24 months or until the city repeals it, whichever comes first.

new_candidates.duration: 90 days from adoption (2026-05-13 through approximately 2026-08-11), passed 4-1.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Leavenworth County Commission resolution, adopted 4-1 at the May 13, 2026 meeting, pausing acceptance of data-center applications in unincorporated county areas and directing planning staff to prepare data-center regulations.
new_candidates.trigger: Project Bluestem, a proposed ~600-megawatt (developer statements later cited up to 1.2-gigawatt) hyperscale data center on 1,000+ acres south of Tonganoxie (Cloverleaf Infrastructure/Tailgate Ranch site), drew sustained community opposition (Citizens Against Bluestem) over noise, air quality, health, and infrastructure concerns.
new_candidates.current_status: Expired 2026-08-11. An extension to Jan. 31, 2027 failed 3-2 at the Aug. 5, 2026 commission meeting; at an Aug. 13, 2026 meeting the commission voted 4-1 to 'revisit' imposing a hold on any decisions until after three new commissioners take office in January 2027, but had not formally re-enacted a moratorium as of the sources retrieved (Sept. 18, 2026 reporting describes Project Bluestem as still in the early stages of the county application process, with no active moratorium mentioned). No applications had been filed for the project as of the sources retrieved.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Project Bluestem (Cloverleaf Infrastructure), a proposed hyperscale data center south of Tonganoxie; no application had been filed as of the sources retrieved.
new_candidates.outcome: 90-day pause on data-center applications in unincorporated Leavenworth County lapsed without a successful extension; three sitting commissioners (two of whom did not seek re-election) opted to defer any renewed pause or decision on Project Bluestem to the incoming commission taking office in January 2027, rather than formally re-adopting a moratorium.

evidence.supports: Details the 90-day moratorium's scheduled expiration, the failed 3-2 extension vote on Aug. 5, 2026, and the Aug. 13, 2026 4-1 vote to revisit a hold before the new commission takes office, without formally re-enacting a moratorium.
evidence.quote: A push to extend a moratorium on data centers in unincorporated areas of the county failed Aug. 5 at a Leavenworth County Commission meeting, but the board now plans to revisit a hold on any plans until after the new commission takes office in January. ... The 90-day moratorium was set to end last week...

evidence.quote: Leavenworth County. The Leavenworth County Commission approved a 90-day moratorium on accepting data-center applications and directed planning staff to prepare data-center regulations; the motion passed 4-1 at the May 13, 2026 meeting.
